problem: Given that $L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}},$ find the Laplace transform $L{{e}^{4t}\cdot {t}^{3}}.$
worked_solution:
The first shifting theorem states that if
$L{f(t)}=F(s),$
then
$L{{e}^{at}f(t)}=F(s-a).$

Using the given result, we have

$$
L{{t}^{3}}=\frac{3!}{{s}^{4}}.
$$

Therefore, applying the first shifting theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}\cdot {t}^{3}} & =\frac{3!}{(s-4)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(s-4)^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
